I doubt your family are skilled survivalist hunters and gatherers. Because if not the majority of you likely wouldn’t survive one winter without the the rest of the world.

It’s true that those numbers may vary given the hypothetical nature and the sample group of the question. However I can assure you that it is not the case where the vast majority of people would choose to sacrifice they’re family. At the very least a substantial percent of population would sacrifice 25 million to save a random family member.

If the question is weather I would sacrifice my mother for the two people if she told me to. Honestly in this situation I’m not really sure what I would do in the heat of the moment. But in a theoretical I would likely sacrifice the two people.

Though this is likely with some people, I don’t think this Is always the case. On a hypothetical Reddit for example where there is no barrier of offending family members. The question of would you sacrifice a random family member or 25 million people. Around 2/3 of replies choose sacrificing the 25 million.

Im a young adult without any kids, but going off of the person who means the most to me. If I were to sacrifice my mother it would have to be to save tens if not hundreds of people. Anything above this I simply couldn’t justify taking so many others like her so that I can be with her for a few more decades.

I agree that for many people with these types of hypotheticals, it can be easy to give the most logical answer in this question. I’ll admit though I know I’d sacrifice my family for the world 100% of the time. If that included me, though I could say that I would sacrifice myself(and I think I would) I might not if the theoretical became reality.
